text:
maya: heads up — ran into a weird auth handoff in the sampleapp when running locally vs CI, cost us a deploy :facepalm:

maya: steps to repro: run sampleapp in docker with REDWOOD_API_KEY set to an org-scoped key + REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY present in CI, but not in local env. locally the app picked the org key and then failed for project-only routes (403). in CI it uses project key and works.

devon: hmm that's bad. can you paste the env vars / config you used?

maya: sure — minimal docker-compose override we use:```yaml
services:
  sample:
    environment:
      - REDWOOD_API_KEY=${REDWOOD_API_KEY}
      - REDWOOD_ORG_KEY=${REDWOOD_ORG_KEY}
      - REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY=${REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY}
```
maya: locally REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY is unset, REDWOOD_API_KEY points at our org token. sampleapp calls /projects/:id/data which requires project scope so api returns 403.

alex: what's the SDK doing for precedence? is REDWOOD_API_KEY considered global and winning over project key?

sam: current SDK auth precedence (from memory): explicit method args > REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY > REDWOOD_ORG_KEY > REDWOOD_API_KEY. but CLI and our sampleapp helper have slightly different fallback order. nasty.

maya: yeah the sampleapp helper apparently checks REDWOOD_API_KEY first (legacy). so mismatch between sampleapp helper and SDK.

jen: can we make behavior deterministic: prefer the most specific (project) when present, and emit a single runtime warning when a broader key is used for a project-only endpoint?

devon: +1. emitting a warning would help catch this without breaking things. maybe a GUID in the warning to make it easier to trace in logs.

sam: quick proposal: change sampleapp helper to call SDK and pass explicit projectKey when REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY env var exists; otherwise fall back. also add unit test to SDK to assert precedence.

alex: also add a small e2e test in CI that runs sampleapp with only org key and asserts 403 for project endpoints — catches regressions.

maya: I'll open a small PR to the sampleapp helper to align with SDK. PR will include repro snippet and a note about rotation implications (when keys rotate, ambiguous env setups are fragile).

devon: assigning review to @jen and @sam. please include changelog note for dev docs: "env var precedence and recommended pattern (project key preferred for project endpoints)"

ci-bot: created pipeline run for branch maya/fix-sampleapp-auth (build #142) :gear:

jen: looking now, thanks. one edgecase — some org tokens have both project and org scopes; if token contains project scope, should it trump a dedicated REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY env var? i'd say explicit env var wins.

sam: agreed: explicit env var wins, then token-scope-inspection to infer project-capability, then fall back to broader. Document that order.

maya: after PR merges i'll also add a short troubleshooting blurb to the developer onboarding doc (sampleapp auth section) showing how to check effective key with `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/whoami`

devon: nice. once merged we should cut a tiny patch to the local docker-compose in quickstarts to demonstrate project-first pattern.

ci-bot: build #142 succeeded. maya/fix-sampleapp-auth merged to main and deployed to staging. :rocket:

maya: deployed to staging — doing a smoke test now.

maya: smoke ok. thanks all. I'll follow up with PR links and the doc blurb. :thumbsup:
